name: Cernunnos

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cernunnos was a Celtic god, one of the most ancient of the Celts. His name and image appear among both continental and insular Celtic peoples. Both go back as far as the fourth century BCE. His name appears in just one inscription from France. The meaning, the horned one, comes from images rather than from language. The image of the horned god appears on the Gundestrup Cauldron. Cernunnos wears the antlers of a stag, not the horns of a farm animal. This links him to the powers of the wildwood. Deer sprout antlers in spring and shed them in autumn. This ties Cernunnos to the seasonal cycle. In nearly every image he appears with animals, both wild and tame. People called him the Master of Animals. He often bears a torc, a symbol of high status. He may stand for abundance and prosperity. He is usually shown with symbols of plenty, such as the cornucopia and the moneybag. No records of his myths survive. His image remains common today. Many think the horned devil image came from Cernunnos.

okr.objective: Cernunnos is an ancient horned Celtic god linked to animals and plenty.
